#3174. Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people new tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.

That’s especially the case when it comes to handing over sensitive financial information. If you give an AI access to your digital wallets to shop for you, the risk extends beyond an authorized purchase. You could be exposing your bank accounts to a potential security breach or data exposure, with little recourse to fix it. If you were considering letting Muse make decisions and transactions with your money ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, you should know it’s still raising red flags as a shopping companion.

Despite the risk, Muse has remained popular and now faces competition from Anthropic’s newly released Claude Duet, another AI business agent. Meta is also releasing a $300 portable device, Charm, in a virtual-toy style that will work with Muse.

A representative for Meta has not responded to CNET’s request for comment.

Muse asks for the keys to your digital life: passwords, full disk access, emails, calendar invites, contacts, Notes and WhatsApp chats. Meta also feeds your conversations into its AI training pipeline by default, leaving it on you to dig through the settings and opt out.

More recently, Meta employees themselves have flagged instances where Muse may have accessed encrypted messages from apps such as Signal or information from other Muse users, which Meta has chalked up to “isolated incidents” and that permission to access apps and information from notifications has to be explicitly granted in a statement to news outlets.

If the previous incidents weren’t enough to give you pause, there’s also a widely publicized case in which Muse mistakenly shared the home address of a Toronto tech reviewer, Matt Robb, with a potential buyer on Facebook Marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

Before facing a potential security nightmare, here are a few other things to know about Muse.

Muse uploads iOS or Mac data even when you tell it not to: Meta’s Muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a September report by AppleInsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off. The report shows that Muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages. Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

Muse could hand over data to human callers: Before Meta launched the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the company planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments. That means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

Muse has the most robust data collection: In September, the VPN company Surfshark said it found that Meta Muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data. Muse (along with Meta AI and Gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset of what it uncovered.

Meta has tried hard with Muse to make the AI agent seem cute and approachable, but when it comes to your money and giving Muse access to it, it’s best to be very cautious for the time being.

#3173. Revolution Medicines Drugged a Target Scientists Called “Undruggable” for Decades. Buy the Stock Hand Over Fist?

Rasonque is off to an impressive start. Here’s what that could mean for Revolution Medicines.

By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 20, 2026 at 3:36PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Revolution Medicines ›

Revolution Medicines (RVMD +1.11%) is living up to its name. Earlier this year, the biotech company earned approval for Rasonque, a medicine for pancreatic cancer that targets one of the main genetic drivers of the disease, the first of its kind to do so. Rasonque's approval was a major milestone, and Revolution Medicines has already been rewarded for it. Shares are up 100% this year. Is there any upside left for the drugmaker?

Many new drugs are tested against a placebo in Phase 3 clinical trials. Being pitted against the standard of care is a much tougher bar to clear. Yet, that's exactly what Rasonque did. In a Phase 3 study, investigators pitted the medicine against cytotoxic chemotherapy, the current standard of care, in patients with previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer.

Rasonque won hands down. It led to a median overall survival of 13.2 months, compared with 6.7 months with cytotoxic chemotherapy. Why is Rasonque so effective? It has a new mechanism of action that targets RAS-addicted cancers (RAS is a protein implicated in the rapid growth of some cancers), which have historically been difficult to treat.

According to Revolution Medicines, RAS-addicted cancers account for between 20% and 30% of all human cancers. So, the company could earn approval for Rasonque and some other candidates in its pipeline across various indications. Revolution Medicines is running eight Phase 3 clinical trials, including several for two other investigational medicines, zoldonrasib and elironrasib. Provided Rasonque experiences a strong commercial ramp-up, and the company makes significant clinical progress over the next few years, Revolution Medicines' shares could maintain strong momentum.

Rasonque earned approval in late August. Yet, in the third quarter, Revolution Medicines generated $198 million in revenue from the medicine, in the roughly five weeks it was on the market before the quarter ended. It was prescribed to more than 5,000 unique patients in the U.S. Some analysts are calling it the strongest launch in the history of the oncology drug market, which is typically dominated by pharmaceutical leaders.

That's impressive, and it highlights the massive opportunity Revolution Medicines is tapping into. That helps put Revolution Medicines' valuation in perspective. The company's current market cap is $34.8 billion, which is quite high for a biotech company that just launched its first product. However, note that Revolution Medicines' stock has declined about 29% since Rasonque's approval, even as the company's initial launch of the drug has crushed expectations.

If anything, Revolution Medicines' third-quarter results show that the market cap it had several months ago, which hovered around $50 billion, may not have been unfounded after all. Consider that some analysts now expect the company to generate $3 billion in revenue next year. Based on this projection, Revolution Medicines is trading at 11.6x estimated 2027 sales.

That's not completely unreasonable for a biotech of this size with a transformative new treatment that could become the standard of care across several oncology indications, the largest market in the pharmaceutical industry. Of course, there is some uncertainty to consider. Revolution Medicines might not make as much next year as some analysts expect.

There is also the possibility of clinical and regulatory setbacks. Even so, Rasonque's trajectory so far, and the fact that clinical progress has been strong -- and Revolution Medicines has a robust pipeline -- make a strong case for the stock. That's especially true since Rasonque recently earned approval in Europe.

And Revolution Medicines will also seek approvals in other countries, including Japan. In my view, the opportunity in the U.S. alone, where Revolution Medicines estimates that about 55,000 new cases of metastatic pancreatic cancer occur annually, justifies its current valuation. So, the stock is worth buying right now and holding onto for at least the next five years.

Don't panic: All your devices should transfer over to Google Home fairly seamlessly.

Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices.

If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has officially confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being sunset, and current users will lose access to both next year.

All Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant.

The change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.”

Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

Google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app.

As part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch.

Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser.

You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

On Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed.

For most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027.

Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

The other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the company starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

Google says Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and users will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information.

Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

Gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google announced earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. Users in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now.

On your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Some of the best Southwest redemptions are only available if you hold one of the airline’s credit cards.

In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

Take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

"Experiences create lifetime memories,” says Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”

Southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but big-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

The event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:

A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

Even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.)

As of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

$1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.)

Four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.)

If you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

Using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

Daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

Ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

Again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

Grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

The biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

You’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

With that said, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

Scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.)

Finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

Southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

But every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

Personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

"We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” says Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

Instead, you probably would've been interested in the 250,000-point package for "Boots, Bourbon and Bonfires" — a three-day trip to Devil's Thumb Ranch, an upscale dude ranch resort about 1.5 hours outside of Denver.

Before you book, just remember: You’ll need a Southwest credit card to purchase.

You want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s important to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:

No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card

Flat-rate travel rewards: Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card

#3167. Geospace (GEOS) Q4 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Backlog tops $100 million as restructuring reshapes the path ahead.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 20, 2026 at 3:53PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Geospace (GEOS -31.42%) reported significant revenue declines and widened net losses for fiscal year 2026, prompting a comprehensive operational restructuring to align costs with a challenging macroeconomic environment. Management stated that global energy disruptions, trade policy shifts, and government procurement delays pressured results across all three business segments. The company entered fiscal year 2027 with a backlog exceeding $100 million and a revised sales strategy for its smart water products to drive a return to profitability.

Operator: Welcome to the Geospace Technologies Fourth Quarter and Year-End 2026 Earnings Conference Call. Hosting the call today from Geospace is Mr. Richard Kelley, President and Chief Executive Officer. He is joined by Mr. Robert Curda, the company's Chief Financial Officer. Today's call is being recorded and will be available on the Geospace Technologies Investor Relations website following the call. [Operator Instructions]. It is now my pleasure to turn the floor over to Richard Kelley. Sir, you may begin.

Richard Kelley: Thank you. Good morning, and welcome to Geospace Technologies conference call for the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026. I am Richard Kelley, the company's President and Chief Executive Officer. I am joined by Robert Curda, the company's Chief Financial Officer. In our prepared remarks, I will first provide an overview of the fourth quarter, and Robert will then follow with more in-depth commentary on our financial performance as well as an overview of our financials for fiscal year 2026. We will then open the line for questions. Today's commentary on markets, revenue, planned operations and capital expenditures may be considered forward-looking as defined by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.

These statements are based on what we know now, but actual outcomes are affected by uncertainties beyond our control or prediction. Both known and unknown risks can lead to results that differ from what is said or implied today. Some of these risks and uncertainties are discussed in our SEC Form 10-K and 10-Q filings. For convenience, we will link a recording of this call on the Investor Relations page of our geospace.com website, which I invite everyone to browse through and learn more about Geospace, our subsidiaries and our products. Note that today's recorded information is time-sensitive and may not be accurate at the time one listens to the replay.

Yesterday, after the market closed, we released our financial results for the period ended September 30, our fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026. For the 3 months ended September 30, 2026, we reported revenue of $19.6 million with a net loss of $13.7 million. For the 12-month period ended September 30, 2026, we reported revenue of $80.7 million with a net loss for the fiscal year at $44.3 million. The global economic situation continue to negatively affect our business. Uncertainty and delays driven by ongoing changes in trade policy, a major Middle East energy disruption, continued sanctions and shifts in borrowing costs negatively impacted our ability to conduct business in our current structure.

As a result, the management team took decisive steps to realign our operations, reduce costs and position Geospace for a return to profitability. During this fiscal year, we implemented 2 reductions in force, and early retirement program and cutbacks in operating expenses to better align our cost structure with today's business environment. Additionally, the challenging business conditions contributed to noncash charges of approximately $6 million of cumulative foreign exchange loss and underutilized equipment charges. Disappointing revenue declines in our Smart Water segment were driven predominantly by decreases in orders for our Hydroconn line of smart water meter connector cables. Broader market conditions point to slower hardware shipments, uneven project deployments and normalization following earlier demand surges.

Several major metering suppliers are experiencing near-term hardware and deployment softness. However, longer-term modernization demand appears more resilient. At the end of the year, we ended a decade-long relationship with an external manufacturing representative firm who had exclusively marketed the Hydroconn connectors. In fiscal year 2027, we will change our market strategy and use internal sales and marketing resources to build demand and secure specifications of our products in utility AMI-related procurements. This approach should reduce expenses associated with representative commissions, increase our control over product promotion and improve insights into customer demand. In addition, we will further leverage our engineering expertise to drive manufacturing efficiencies.

While the contribution from the Aquana brand remains modest, the products continue to grow with year-over-year revenue increases. In the coming year, we look to build upon the growth in Aquana revenue and maximize our early efforts with white label product manufacturing to support a revenue expansion in this segment. The impacts of energy market volatility, shifts in project timing, increased component and shipping costs as well as access to raw materials negatively impacted our Energy Solutions segment. Increased competition and consolidation remain challenging in the marine exploration market and have led to decreased demand for ocean bottom nodes.

The segment focused resources on execution of sizable contracts, including the Petrobras's Permanent Reservoir Monitoring or PRM program, which is expected to be shipped and product-related revenue recognized by the end of fiscal year 2027. The global conditions proved harshest for our energy sales efforts. However, we have a strong backlog in this segment going into next fiscal year. Long-term demand forecast should drive more favorable land exploration market conditions resulting in additional Pioneer contracts. For the Intelligent Industrial segment, the economic headwinds were less severe, but still influenced revenue timing. The biggest factor impacting revenue generation was government procurement timing at both state and federal levels.

After a lengthy effort and as previously announced, our Quantum Technology Sciences subsidiary entered into a $10.8 million contract with the U.S. Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane division for the company's Seismic Acoustic Detection and Ranging Underwater System. We anticipate revenue recognition from the project to span fiscal years 2027 and 2028. Similar timing delays have occurred around the sale of the Heartbeat Detector, a vehicle security screening technology used globally by correctional facilities, corporate security and border agencies. Lengthy procurement cycles and complex approvals have resulted in slower-than-expected revenue recognition with this product line, but the outlook and demand for the technology remains extremely encouraging.

While it has been an incredibly challenging year for the company, efforts to better align our company's cost structure with today's business environment should place the company on a path to profitability in fiscal year 2027. We entered fiscal year 2027 with a backlog exceeding $100 million from contracts across our 3 segments. Contributions to the backlog encompass not only the PRM program, but contracts with the U.S. federal government and other agencies as well as contract manufacturing customers and smart water white label commitments. The strong backlog as well as an accretive acquisition strategy and restructured operations position Geospace for success in future periods.

We will continue to execute our strategic priorities by investing in innovation, supporting our customers and maintaining financial discipline. Our focus remains on converting the opportunities within our pipeline into revenue, improving operating performance and positioning the company for long-term profitable growth. I will now turn the call over to Robert to provide more detail on our financial performance.

Robert Curda: Thanks, Richard, and good morning. Before I begin, I'd like to remind everyone that we will not provide any specific revenue or earnings guidance during our call this morning. In yesterday's press release for our fourth quarter ended September 30, 2026, we reported revenue of $19.6 million compared to last year's revenue of $30.7 million. The net loss for the quarter was $13.7 million or $1.06 per diluted share compared to last year's net loss of $9.1 million or $0.71 per diluted share. Our fourth quarter loss include noncash charges of $3.5 million in cumulative translation losses from our Colombian operation and $2.9 million of underutilized assets related to select nodal rental tools and manufacturing equipment.

For the 12 months ended September 30, 2026, we reported revenue of $80.7 million compared to revenue of $110.8 million last year. Our net loss for the 12-month period was $44.3 million or $3.43 per diluted share compared to last year's net loss of $9.7 million or $0.76 per diluted share. Revenue from our Smart Water segment totaled $3.1 million for the 3 months ended September 30, 2026. This compares to $8.5 million in revenue for the same prior year period, a decrease of 63%. For the fiscal year, revenue from this segment totaled $17.2 million versus $35.8 million for the same prior year period for a decrease of 52%.

The decrease in revenue for the 3-month and 12-month periods is due to a decrease in demand for our Hydroconn Universal AMI connectors. For the 3-month period ended September 30, 2026, revenue from our Energy Solutions segment totaled $10.8 million for a decrease of 31% when compared to $15.7 million from the same prior year period. Revenue from the 12-month period was $40.9 million, a decrease of 19% when compared to revenue from the same prior year period of $50.7 million.

The decrease for the 3-month period and 12-month period is due to lower utilization and sales of our marine ocean bottom node rental fleet, partially offset by revenue recognized related to performance on our PRM contract and sales of the Pioneer. Revenue from our Intelligent Industrial segment totaled $5.6 million for the 3-month period ended September 30, 2026. This compares with $6.4 million from the equivalent year ago period, representing a decrease of 12%. Revenue for the 12 months was $22.2 million. This compares to the prior year ago period of $24 million, a decrease of 7%.

The decrease in revenue for the 3-month period and 12-month period was due to lower demand for our industrial sensors and imaging products, partially offset by an increase in security and defense revenue. Our 12-month cash investments into our current plant and equipment are $4 million. At September 30, we had working capital of $43.6 million, which includes $14 million of trade accounts and financing receivables. On October 29, we entered into a revolving loan and security agreement with Amerisource Funding Inc., restructuring and terminating our Woodforest credit agreement. At this time, we have approximately $13 million of available borrowings under the Amerisource agreement. That concludes my discussion, and I'll now return the call to Richard for his closing comments.

Richard Kelley: Thank you, Robert. This concludes our prepared commentary, and I will now turn the call back to the moderator for any questions from our listeners.

Operator: [Operator Instructions]. And we'll take our first question from Isaac Pommer with Tieton Capital Management.

Isaac Pommer: I'd like to start with Petrobras and kind of just asking about what was the revenue for that part in the September quarter, if you're able to kind of talk about that?

Richard Kelley: Robert, do you want to fill that question?

Robert Curda: Yes. It wasn't that significant. It's about $6.5 million.

Isaac Pommer: Okay. And then is there kind of revenue expected in kind of the December quarter that's probably maybe a little bit more of what -- I don't know, a little bit more of a percentage than the 6%?

Richard Kelley: Yes. I think -- so we are in full production now. And so based on the fact that we can recognize revenue for completions, we anticipate revenue recognition in our fiscal Q1 and Q2 and Q3. So as I stated, we should recognize the majority of the goods revenue associated with that contract in the fiscal year.

Robert Curda: Yes. It should continue to grow and come to its peak in our Q2 and come to an end in Q3.

Isaac Pommer: That's really helpful. And pivoting now to the PRMs. Are there any public or private PRM tenders today?

Richard Kelley: None that we're discussing now.

Isaac Pommer: Okay. Are you able to like talk about any perspective in the coming months? Or is that also you're not talking about?

Richard Kelley: Yes. I mean everything we discuss with our clients is considered confidential until they actually make it public. So we're not able to make a comment at this time.

Isaac Pommer: Okay. That sounds good. And then I also just wanted to ask another question about the cost-saving measures. Richard Kelley: So we reduced our overhead -- overall headcount by over 10% in fiscal year 2026. We took a number of cost-cutting measures on our operating expenses as well. We had commented on that actually in the previous quarter. We're also utilizing a lot of AI productivity tools to try to reduce the amount of manual labor within the organization. So we anticipate our cost structure to become even more aligned with where we're at from a revenue standpoint in subsequent quarters.

Isaac Pommer: Okay. That's really helpful. And then I kind of just want to ask about -- I know you said you weren't going to give a lot of guidance or any guidance into the coming months. But can I just ask about -- is December quarter kind of look similar or different to this September quarter that you just reported? Is there any like swing factors that you're seeing that may be a little bit different to kind of look out for?

Richard Kelley: I would say that our anticipation for Q1 is similar to what we've experienced in prior Q1, at the end of the year. So we do see a bit of a softening in demand. So we anticipate I wouldn't say as bad as it is this quarter, but I would say that our real expectation for returning profitability would be closer to Q2 and Q3. So flattish, I would say, is probably the best guidance I can give. More profitability in Q2 and Q3 with our intent to return to full profitability by the end of the fiscal year.

Isaac Pommer: Okay. Yes, that's helpful. And then can you give some more insights or some comments that we should see around additional Pioneer contracts?

Richard Kelley: Yes. I mean we still see good demand for the solution. We've made several announcements about units that we've sold. One of our largest customers is seeing good demand for their services in the Lower 48. The technology is proven now in the field. It's very well received. Isaac Pommer: Yes. That's really great to hear. And then just one final question I have, and then I'll step back. Just you're getting back to profitability. Richard Kelley: Sure. I mean we're working both the top line and below the line, right? So the sales team is focused on chasing every opportunity for revenue. That's a very tenuous period of time to say we'll be there in 6 months.

Richard Kelley: No, I don't disagree with you. As we had mentioned in prior quarters, Petrobras had made some changes to the design, which led to delays in our ability to get going. That's all behind us. That's all been resolved. As I mentioned, we are in full production now. And one of the things we're dealing with international -- large international companies is they don't really change their contracts for small suppliers. They anticipate you to be flexible for that. And even though we have a good working relationship with Petrobras, and we've been in constant communication with them, the reality is until we hit that milestone, we can't expect another infusion of cash.

And so we are working very hard and very diligently to achieve that next milestone.

Robert Curda: We also only have $0.5 million in debt at September 30, and we have available borrowings of $13 million.

Michael Cox: Well, maybe unpack that further, you say it's a $25 million facility. And as of right now, you have available borrowings of $13 million that implication is that you've drawn half of the facility. Is that an incorrect assumption?

Robert Curda: No, that's not correct. There's limitations on the borrowing base. It's a borrowing base calculation. So while there's a max of $25 million available at a given time, we may not have the base available to borrow the full amount, okay?

Michael Cox: Okay. Thank you for the clarification on that. Okay. The -- all right. That's helpful. The smart water change in terms of how you're selling the product, I understand that the opportunity exists now to earn -- to not pay out as much in commissions to third-party sales, but you're also now shifting a variable expense to a fixed one and by building out an internal team, which seems like an interesting point in time to be doing that. Can you talk about what it takes in terms of the fixed cost it would take to build your internal team and shed the external one?

Richard Kelley: Sure. So we plan to leverage our Aquana expertise. And we already have a sales team in that space that deals with municipalities. But in a larger sense, what we've done in the last few years is really build a strong relationship with the OEMs themselves. And so we're working to make sure that we -- our connector is the connector of choice even for them where we've managed to put our pricing structure where it's competitive to where they're currently sourcing if they're sourcing their prioritized connector out overseas. So we are able to offset some of the losses with new projects and new customer base.

So between working with the OEMs and then leveraging our Aquana sales team with regards to municipalities and driving specifications and things like that, we think that the additional need for people on that team and expertise in that team is not as much as it may seem from the outside. So we know which municipalities we really need to go after.

So between focused marketing, adding a couple of people, leveraging our Aquana sales team and our relationship with the OEMs, I think we'll be in a pretty good position at least for the next year and rolling that out.

Michael Cox: Okay. All right. Sorry, I can't come back to the cash thing for one more swing. And the -- so $13 million of availability, really not going to receive a cash infusion from Petrobras until sometime around Q2. In the past, we talked about you have some properties you could sell. You have some -- there were other things that you could do. I haven't heard mention of those in a while, but what is the plan B?

Robert Curda: We're continuing to evaluate those options. We look at them continuously, and they're definitely not off the table.

Operator: We will take our next question from Sheldon Grodsky with Grodsky.

Sheldon Grodsky: I'll continue with some questions regarding your liquidity.

Richard Kelley: Sheldon, I'm sorry, I can barely hear you.

Sheldon Grodsky: Is this better let me -- any better?

Sheldon Grodsky: Okay. What I said was I was -- I'm going to continue with questions regarding liquidity. You have some financing receivables. When are they supposed to be paid?

Richard Kelley: Robert, do you want to address that?

Robert Curda: Yes. The majority of the financing receivables we have a maturity of about 24 months left on them.

Sheldon Grodsky: Okay. No chance that could be hurried up if necessary?

Robert Curda: As other options to fortify our liquidity, that's actually one of the ones that's on the table also.

Sheldon Grodsky: Okay. Now you also have an almost fully depreciated rental equipment fleet. So that your depreciation is going to be going down. And since the value of the assets is close to 0, you'd be getting gains whenever you sold it. Are you planning to stay in the leasing business, the rental business? Richard Kelley: I mean we certainly still plan to be in the rental equipment business for marine nodes. I mean we've made that position clear. There is still opportunities for that. So we do intend to -- and I have to be careful.

On the rental fleet, as we've reported in prior periods, the older legacy equipment, the OBX product line, we are phasing that out, and we anticipate standardizing around the Mariner solution for going forward. So we continue to try to sell off the legacy equipment if there's opportunities for that. And then we will build our -- we have a small rental pool available at Mariner, and we will build that out as demand builds. So we continue to monitor that. But we do anticipate remaining in that business.

Sheldon Grodsky: You also have this -- you have long had this noncurrent inventory balance, which is shrinking. Is there any way that, that can be converted to cash fairly quickly?

Richard Kelley: Not quickly. I mean our sales team is aware of what we have on the shelf. We work pretty regularly on putting that in front of our legacy or historical customers who have bought the equipment in the past to see what the potential demand would be for that. But the reality is that the markets that, that equipment is in have softened, and it's -- customers are buying it as they need it, but they're not buying in anticipation of a strategic move in any way.

Sheldon Grodsky: Okay. By the way, in the message to investors, you mentioned acquisition strategy. I would assume that under the present circumstances that the acquisitions are not likely and may not be permissible under your credit agreement. So can you make any comments about the likelihood of acquisitions under your credit agreement?

Robert Curda: Yes. Our current credit agreement doesn't prohibit us for making acquisitions.

Sheldon Grodsky: Would they have to approve it?

Robert Curda: Off the top of my head, I don't remember that, but I would certainly discuss it with them.

Operator: And we'll take a question from Glenn Kukla with Kukla Capital Partners.

Glenn Kukla: Glenn here, big fan still. A couple of quick questions. The -- let's talk about Petrobras. Are you able to comment about their satisfaction? Can you give us any color on the performance of the PRM project to date? And more importantly, are you able to discuss how confident they might be on future PRM projects?

Richard Kelley: Yes, it's fine. With regards to Petrobras and our relationship with Petrobras, I would say we are in good standing with them. We meet with them very regularly, 2 or 3 times a week between technical discussions and project updates. And they have been in our facility recently. In fact, we had a representative last week monitoring our progress. And I think overall, I would say that they're satisfied with where we're at in the project and making -- meeting their needs. With regards to the technology, obviously, they're quite happy about the technology or they wouldn't have awarded us the contract, obviously.

And with regards to their future plans, I mean, I think Petrobras has made plenty of comments about their full buy-in to the value of permanent reservoir monitoring. They have PRM on some older fields that they've been using for a number of years now. They just installed the system on Mero 1 and 2. So I think that they're long-term committed to that. I think their overall strategy on their field management lends itself to PRM, but they have not made any announcements publicly about any future plans they have other than that they do anticipate using PRM on the fields going forward.

Glenn Kukla: Got you. Just trying to trying to characterize how much they love Geospace?

Richard Kelley: I wish I could put a number on that. I really do. I will say that every time we talk to them, though, I mean, they don't really bring up anything negative or any concerns about Geospace as a company or our technology.

Glenn Kukla: Okay. Landscape for other PRM tenders with other entities, companies, countries, whereas you certainly shouldn't and cannot talk about any ongoing discussions. Are you able to characterize what kind of appetite is out there for Petrobras' cohorts, appetite for potential OptoSeis systems?

Richard Kelley: Yes. I mean, as you said, I can't talk any specifics, but I can talk about the general landscape. I would say -- and I've mentioned this in prior calls, national oil companies where it's much more strategic long-term management of their reservoir and trying to optimize performance, I think that PRM makes a lot of sense for those types of reservoirs. I think the majors, the independent oil companies, they have a lot of -- they have different levers that they have to pull with regards to how they allocate their capital resources. And PRM has a longer payback than an ocean bottom node survey and their position can change on reservoirs.

So I think it's a different story we have to tell for them as far as the value creation and the value add for the PRM to them. And I would say in the fields of interest, so if you look north of Brazil, Guyana, obviously, would be an example, North Sea, Equinor has PRM systems on their reservoirs. Now their overall strategy change with renewables and just like all the other kind of oil companies did. But I think we're seeing a swing back to recognizing that hydrocarbons play an important role going forward. So there's some opportunity there. And of course, West Africa looks really interesting, right?

I mean West Africa geologically is very similar to Brazil and Guyana. And so I mean -- and that's why we see a lot of exploration going on, on West Africa. But there, the challenge is going to be geopolitics, right? I mean it's not quite as stable there and funding is more complex there. But there's certainly opportunities for PRM on some of these basins outside of where we're at today in Brazil.

Glenn Kukla: Okay. And are any of these companies hungry now? Or is this sort of an appetite you might see roll out later in the future...

Richard Kelley: Yes. I think these are probably more mid- to longer-term prospects. Right now, short term, I think -- especially if you look at Africa, I think it's really just a question of understanding what they have and how they manage it so. And Guyana, they just -- I don't want to really comment too much on Guyana. But if you look at the players there, there was a lot of legal back and forth in the recent years about that. So I think they're just now really starting to get into a stable point where they can make longer-term decisions around that reservoir.

Glenn Kukla: Okay. You alluded to growth lever acquisition and the previous caller talked about how to fund that. I'm not as concerned about funding it, but rather if you're out there with your elephant gun looking to hunt animal, hunt acquisition, what do those technologies look like? What are we looking to hunt for? What's our appetite?

Richard Kelley: No, that's a great question. And as we've honed -- we really just started the sort of active acquisition effort in the last kind of 18 months. We have a dedicated business development person, and we had a partner that was kind of on working with us to identify opportunities. I would say that the drivers for us is can they be accretive short term to the company. So trying to stay away from start-ups unless the technology is phenomenal and has really big benefits. And we're also looking at -- we started focusing on smart water. Smart water is still a priority for us.

But if there's an acquisition of opportunity that's in Energy or in Intelligent Industrial that meets our goals of being accretive, some sort of recurring revenue model that makes sense for us and that we can fold in fairly easily into our engineering team and into our back-office support team, then we'll take a good hard look at it.

Glenn Kukla: Great. Would Heartbeat be an example of the type of acquisition you'd be looking to do again?

Richard Kelley: Yes. I think that something that's out there proven, but they've upgraded their technology are offered a really interesting solution above what they had before, fairly small footprint, a really interesting recurring revenue story and in a very niche market where there's not a lot of competition from a technology standpoint, I think those are -- that's a great outline for us. Now as far as size, that was a fairly small acquisition. I think we could look for something maybe a little bit bigger than that. But as the previous call alluded to, I mean, our financial situation also kind of handcuffs a little bit for trying to make large deals.

Glenn Kukla: Yes. Hopefully, that will change, and you'll get more powder in the bag.

Richard Kelley: That's our -- that is what we're working towards, right? And that's kind of the message I was trying to convey is we are -- even though we want to grow, we are taking a hard look at how we stand today with regards to our current markets and make sure that we're sized appropriately, so that we can at least get close or at profitability or even improve profitability by the end of fiscal year 2027.

Glenn Kukla: Great. That dovetails my last question. I'm going to put you on the spot, but I'm also going to say you don't even have to answer this. 24 months from now, is Geospace a going concern?

Richard Kelley: Absolutely. Yes. We feel very good about fiscal year '27 and the opportunities we have going to fiscal year '28. We've had some great conversations with our partners as far as what their plans are over the next 18 to 24 months. We're in the mix for those, and we feel very good about them. One large caveat. We just have through an election cycle, and that can change the dynamics. So we are closely monitoring the geopolitics, both domestically and internationally and see how that impacts our markets.

Richard Kelley: Yes, it's good to hear from you.

Operator: We'll take a follow-up from Michael Cox.

Michael Cox: Yes, just 2 quickies. One, you talk about your conversations with Petrobras 2 to 3 times a week, which is great. And I know that they are a giant company. But are they aware of your cash situation? And are they expressing any concern about the ability for you to deliver given the relatively little amount of cash you have left to get from here to Q3, Q2?

Richard Kelley: Yes. I would say that Petrobras is aware of where we're at. And I would say that we've had much more detailed conversations under confidentiality with them as far as how we plan to bridge that, and they're comfortable with where we're at today.

Michael Cox: And then, you throw out a caveat just a second ago about the political environment. And I guess perhaps I'm not sure whether you're foreshadowing something negative or positive, but I think we all thought 2 years ago that the political environment was going to be good for Geospace and it has actually turned out to be a disaster. So do you have any preliminary views on what's happening? I just asked for, I mean, we all thought Quantum was going to get a chance to have a border security product and in fact, you never even got a chance. And then obviously, everything that's going on in the Middle East has been horrible.

So this has actually been 2 of the worst years I can imagine for you guys. So I mean, can it get worse politically?

Richard Kelley: Well, that's the thing that is the question, right? I mean, how does this administration respond to having tremendous oversight? What is that -- can we bring the Middle East to a conclusion sooner rather than later and get operations back going in that space? What does that mean for infrastructure within the smart water space? I mean these are all questions that we don't have answers to, but we're monitoring closely. And we're trying to be able to be responsive and reactive as quickly as we can to those changes in the market. Your point is valid. I mean, we thought that with this administration, with the focus on immigration and border security that we would see an opportunity.

We couldn't have anticipated that they would have been a direct award to our competitor without really a chance to even bid on it. And -- but I would say that in response to that, we have talked to the other party that was involved, and there's -- there might be some opportunities there, and we try to pursue those. And we try to be responsive to the changes in that market dynamic. Same is true on the Energy side. We're trying to find other paths, other areas where energy -- and the Lower 48 has picked up. This administration's push to be energy independent has led to increased production.

And I think our partners in that space have seen some growth from that. And so they have -- I mean there's no way we could have seen 2 years ago how bad fiscal year '26 would have been, not even 18 months ago. And what we've done as a management team is try to control the things that we can control, right? We can't control these things. All we can do is be aware of them and formulate a strategy for how we can respond to them as quickly as possible.

Unfortunately, there's -- we are embedded in some of these markets, and it's hard for us to pivot away from them quickly, but we are working to do that going forward.

Operator: And it does appear that there are no further questions at this time. I would now like to hand back to Richard Kelley for any additional or closing remarks.

Richard Kelley: Thank you, Chloe, and thanks to all of you who joined our call today. We look forward to speaking with you again on our conference call for the first quarter of fiscal year 2027. Have a great day. Goodbye.

Operator: Thank you. This brings us to the end of today's meeting. We appreciate your time and participation. You may now disconnect.

#3166. What to Buy (and Skip) on Black Friday 2026

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

Electronics, small appliances, toys and clothes make the list, along with some out-of-the-box buys.

Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The big day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.)

You don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, says Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”

Non-electronic toys are a good bet, says Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

NeeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold says.

While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

“Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”

Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley says.

Got some counter space and an itch for a new food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

“Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath says. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”

Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold says.

Electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath says.

Gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath says. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”

That said, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold says.

For best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, says consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after New Year’s Day.

“Big-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold says.

Many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath says. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

Shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold says. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

Just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath says. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”

One caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch says. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:

Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

Fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch says.

Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:

Let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch says. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.)

Check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley says. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”

Use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

#3165. Analysts See 40% Boost for Take-Two Stock on Blowout Grand Theft Auto VI Sales. Are They Right?

Wells Fargo's analyst anticipates Take-Two will rake in $9.76 billion in net bookings this fiscal year, 20% more than the video game maker's own guidance.

By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 20, 2026 at 3:55PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Take-Two Interactive Software ›

The reviews are in for Grand Theft Auto VI, and they are glowing. The reviewer for the gaming publication IGN called it "the single most impressive video game I have ever played."

Gamespot's review called it "an astonishing open-world action game that I'd wager won't be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7."

Metacritic gave it a score of 99 out of 100 based on 151 critic reviews -- the site's highest score ever.

Wall Street is also blown away by the revenue-generating potential of GTA VI and is bullish on Take-Two Interactive (TTWO +0.65%), the company that produces GTA VI. Of the 31 analysts who cover Take-Two stock, 97% rate it as a buy with a median price target of $290 per share, implying 39% upside from its current price.

According to the company, GTA VI sold 32.5 million copies of the game during the pre-sale period, a record. And including pre-sales and sales on the first day it was available to buy on Nov. 19, the game generated $3.79 billion in sales.

That is a one-day record for the entertainment industry across any medium, the company said. This was significanly higher than the projected pre-sale totals and the one-day net revenue projections by industry trackers. The sales numbers already cover the gameʻs production and marketing costs, estimated at $1 billion to $1.5 billion.

Take-Two Interactive expects between $8 billion and $8.2 billion in net bookings this fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. Net bookings refer to revenue from both games sold and in-game purchases. That would be about 21% higher, at the midpoint, than the $6.7 billion in net bookings it saw last fiscal year.

But one Wall Street analyst sees Take-Two blowing past that estimate.

This week, analysts at Wells Fargo (WFC -2.47%) updated their sales projections for Take-Two in light of the pre-sales and sales trends for GTA VI.

Wells Fargo anticipates that GTA VI will sell 65 million copies by the end of Take-Two's fiscal 2027 on March 31. Based on its forecasts, Wells Fargo projects net bookings this fiscal year to be $9.76 billion. That's 19% higher than previous estimates and some $1.6 billion, or 20%, more than Take-Two's own guidance at the midpoint.

The estimate anticipates a significant boost coming from the release of the PC and online versions of GTA VI in early 2027. Currently, only the single-player version of the game has been released. The online version is the multiplayer game. According to reports, GTA V, which came out in 2013, still generates about $500 million per year from the multiplayer game, so it goes without saying that GTA VI online will be a massive sales boost.

Analysts at Wedbush estimate sales of 30 million to 40 million copies by the end of calendar 2026. That would beat the roughly 29 million copies GTA V sold in the first month after its release in 2013. GTA V went on to sell some 235 million copies, making it the second best-selling game of all time.

In its guidance, Take-Two calls for net bookings of $3.35 billion to $3.5 billion in its fiscal 2027 Q3, which ends Dec. 31, and revenue of $3.27 billion to $3.42 billion. That would be up from net bookings of $1.76 billion and revenue of $1.7 billion in fiscal 2026 Q3.

That's why investors should expect GTA VI to provide a strong multiyear boost to revenue and earnings. It's a game that takes 100 or more hours to complete, doing all the side quests, so it will engage players for a long time and prompt in-game purchases. Plus, when the multiplayer game comes out next year, it will generate recurring revenue as players go through the game multiple times with friends and others, and make in-game purchases. The $500 million in annual revenue from GTA V is testament to that.

Take-Two stock had a 25% run-up the week before the Nov. 19 release to $230 per share and has since settled back down to around $208 per share in a sell-the-news scenario. But that just makes for a better entry price.

Take-Two stock is reasonably valued at 28 times forward earnings and is a solid buy right now. GTA VI should generate strong revenue and boost earnings not just this fiscal year, but in the years ahead, as GTA V did following its release in 2013. Over the last 10 years, Take-Two stock has posted an average annualized return of 16%.

#3164. Here's How Many Shares of Procter & Gamble You'd Need for $1,000 in Yearly Dividends

The consumer goods leader is one of the best dividend stocks investors can own.

By Neil Patel – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:00PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Procter & Gamble ›

Procter & Gamble (PG +0.91%)shares have climbed only 103% in the past 10 years (as of Nov. 13). The company certainly isn't drawing in growth investors, but it can be a top choice for income seekers.

Here's how many shares of this consumer staples stock you would need to generate $1,000 in yearly dividends.

Procter & Gamble currently pays a quarterly dividend of $1.0885 per share, which amounts to $4.354 on an annualized basis. This means you would have to own 230 shares to collect $1,000 in yearly passive income. At the current stock price of $169.83, the investment required totals over $39,000.

At 2.56%, the dividend yield is healthy. That's much higher than what the S&P 500 index (^GSPC -3.70%) offers.

Investors should be blown away by the payout's durability. In April, the board of directors raised the dividend, which marked the 70th straight year that a hike was approved. What’s more, the business has paid dividends in 136 consecutive years, a mind-boggling track record.

Shareholders can sleep well at night knowing that their income stream is safe. Procter & Gamble reports sizable earnings, with an operating margin in the first quarter of 2027 (ended Sept. 30) of 25.5%, that results in meaningful free cash flow. The company has also stood the test of time, a sign that its products have stable demand throughout various economic scenarios.

The stock isn't a home run. It's a safe portfolio addition, however.

#3163. Mortgage Rates Today, Thursday, November 19: Kind of a Big Jump

We believe everyone should be able to make financial decisions with confidence. While we don't cover every company or financial product on the market, we work hard to share a wide range of offers and objective editorial perspectives.

So how do we make money? Our partners compensate us for advertisements that appear on our site. This compensation helps us provide tools and services - like free credit score access and monitoring. With the exception of mortgage, home equity and other home-lending products or services, partner compensation is one of several factors that may affect which products we highlight and where they appear on our site. Other factors include your credit profile, product availability and proprietary website methodologies.

However, these factors do not influence our editors' opinions or ratings, which are based on independent research and analysis. Our partners cannot pay us to guarantee favorable reviews. Here is a list of our partners.

TL;DR: Mortgage rates rose enough today that you might be feeling some sticker shock.

If you're here looking for lower mortgage interest rates, today is definitely not your day.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points higher than yesterday and 12 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

Keep in mind that mortgage rates are always on the move, and that if you're tracking rates day-to-day, you're going to see a lot of volatility. Zooming out and looking at the bigger picture — like a graph showing at least a month's worth of rate data — can help you see the overall trend.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

On Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

Investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

» MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there aren’t many people for whom that’s true.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

» Stay informed: Check out NerdWallet's mortgage news hub for all our latest coverage.

The rate you see advertised is a sample rate — usually for a borrower with perfect credit, making a big down payment, and paying for mortgage points. That won't match every buyer's circumstances.

In addition to market factors outside of your control, your customized quote depends on your:

Even two people with similar credit scores might get different rates, depending on their overall financial profiles.

» Get the best rate for you: How to get the best mortgage rate

Maybe — but even personalized rate quotes can change until you lock. That’s because lenders adjust pricing multiple times a day in response to market changes.
