#3150. WeRide (WRD) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Overseas revenue jumped 171% as Robotaxi fleet growth reshaped the story.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:24PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

WeRide (WRD -8.58%) reported significant expansion in its international L4 autonomous driving operations and achieved positive unit economics for its Robotaxi fleet in Guangzhou. Management highlighted the scaling of its asset-light partnership model with platforms such as Uber and the growth of its Jingshuo subsidiary in the AI infrastructure sector. The company stated that it is fully funded to achieve positive free cash flow by 2029 through its existing cash reserves and narrowing operational losses.

Operator: Morning and good evening, ladies and gentlemen. Thank you for standing by, and welcome to WeRide's third quarter 2026 earnings conference call. Please note that today's event is being recorded. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. For today's call, management will use English as the main language. A third-party interpreter will provide simultaneous Chinese interpretation. The company will be hosting a question-and-answer session after management prepare remarks. If you wish to listen to management's original statements or ask a question during the question-and-answer session, please make sure you are dialed in to the English language line. Please note that the Chinese interpretation is for convenience purposes only.

In the case of any discrepancy, management's statements in their original language will prevail. Joining us today are WeRide's Founder, Chairman, and CEO, Dr. Xu Han, and CFO and Head of International, Ms. Xuan Li. Before we continue, I would like to refer you to the safe harbor statement in the company's earnings press release, which also applies to this call, as today's call will include forward-looking statements, including WeRide's strategies and future plans. These forward-looking statements are made under the safe harbor provisions of the U.S. Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties.

The company's actual results could differ materially from those stated or implied by these forward-looking statements as a result of various important factors, and please refer to the risk factor section of the company's Form 20-F filed with the SEC and announcements on the website of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange for a full disclosure of these risk factors. The company does not assume any obligation to update any forward-looking statements except as required under applicable law.

Please note that all numbers stated in management's prepared remarks are in RMB terms, and we will discuss non-IFRS measures today, which are more thoroughly explained and reconciled to the most comparable measures reported in the company's earnings release and filings with the SEC and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The company's unaudited financial and operating results were released earlier today via newswire and can be found on the company's IR website. With that, we will now begin with the company's video presentation.

Head: [Presentation] [Presentation] [Presentation]

Operator: I would like to pass the floor to the company's founder, chairman, and CEO, Dr. Xu Han. Please go ahead, sir.

Xu Han: Thank you. Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining the third quarter earnings call, WeRide. We delivered a very strong quarter, beating market expectations with larger revenue and less net loss. Our revenue grew by 88% year-over-year to CNY 321.5 million, and the gross margin improved to 43%, driven primarily by our high-margin overseas business. Comparing to last quarter, our net loss narrowed by 22.6% to CNY 310 million. We are growing fast and becoming more efficient at the same time. I want to highlight that our Robotaxi revenue grew by 204% year-over-year, of which 90% comes from overseas market. Currently, WeRide is Uber's largest fully driverless Robotaxi partner outside the U.S.

Moreover, revenue from our AI infrastructure segment nearly doubled as we capture rapidly growing demand for physical AI. The subsidiary of WeRide, Jingshuo, now has several billion RMB worth of orders and a framework agreement. At the operational level, our L4 fleet reached about 4,100 vehicles, and our Robotaxi fleet has surpassed 2,300 vehicles. In China, we achieved positive unit economics per Robotaxi in Guangzhou. In Middle East, our fleet size reached 600 vehicles, representing a 50% increase. In Europe, we received Spain's first national operating permit for L4 autonomous passenger vehicles, and we expect to launch commercial operations by year-end. This sets a benchmark for our commercial rollout across Europe.

We are on track toward our goal of deploying tens of thousands of Robotaxis in Europe before 2030. Before I dive into details, I want to address a few topics that our investors care most. First, losses and cash. Investors have asked whether our growth comes at the cost of rising losses. The answer is no. Our revenue grew by 39% quarter-on-quarter, and the gross profit grew by 59%. Our net loss narrowed by 22.6% quarter-on-quarter to CNY 310 million, better than market expectations. We ended the quarter with about CNY 4.7 billion in cash reserves, which fully funds our plan to reach positive quarterly free cash flow in 2028. Xuan will walk through our cash positions in detail.

Second, the quality of our growth. Our revenue base is becoming increasingly recurring. Service revenue, which includes Robotaxi operating service fees, rose 102% year-over-year and now accounts for 58% of total revenue. This revenue stream scales with every ride, delivers high margins, and requires no vehicle ownership on our part. Third, our international business. Overseas revenue rose 171.5% and now accounts for nearly half of our total revenue, as well as over 90% of our Robotaxi revenue. Our Middle East fleet expanded 50% in a single quarter. We launched public Robotaxi services in Zurich, and Spain awarded us its first national L4 operating permit. Permits take years to secure and represent one of the hardest-to-replicate moats in this business.

We collaborate with multiple platform and fleet partners, including Uber, Grab, and several local platforms, which diversifies our channels and make our growth more resilient. Fourth, about AI infrastructure. Some investors have asked whether Jingshuo, our subsidiary, is a distraction from our L4 efforts. It is not. Jingshuo monetizes the data and the tooling we already built for our own autonomous driving operations. It is an asset-light data powerhouse with robust growth momentum. Its revenue nearly doubled this quarter, and it has several billion RMB worth of orders under framework agreement. I will revisit each of these points as I work through the quarter. Let us review the overall results. Both revenue and the gross margin delivered substantial growth.

Revenue rose 38.8% quarter-on-quarter, and the gross margin expanded by 5.5 percentage points sequentially. Overseas market were the primary growth driver. Our revenues climbed 171.5% year-over-year and accounted for nearly half of total revenue. Quarterly Robotaxi revenue exceed CNY 100 million, up 204% year-over-year. More importantly, high-margin overseas market accounted for over 90% of this revenue. Within the AI infrastructure segment, we have built a substantial library of high-quality real-world dataset for physical AI, expanding our capabilities from autonomous vehicles to robotics. For the ADAS segment, our L2++/L3 business, cumulative deliveries surpassed 100,000 units at the quarter end. This means we have hit our full-year target ahead of schedule.

In addition, we secured 10 new mass production design wins and formed new partnerships with several leading OEMs. Going forward, we will advance our physical AI strategy and accelerate L4 fleet scaling and expansion. Now let me talk about our strategy. Investors have also asked about our long-term strategy. They want to understand the strategic positioning of each business and how we allocate our resources. I want to emphasize that WeRide has evolved from an autonomous driving company into a physical AI company. WeRide now project our capability and value in physical AI onto several application dimensions, including L4 dimension, the Robotaxi, L2++/L3 dimension, the ADAS application, and AI infrastructure dimensions, the model services.

Our subsidiary, Jingshuo, focuses on real-world data collection, labeling, simulation, and the related model services. It now covers multimodal data and the complex scenarios. This forms an underlying data and a model engine for physical AI. To summary, Jingshuo is the projection of physical AI company WeRide in AI infrastructure dimension. Today, we bring our capabilities and value in physical AI to market mainly through our L4 business. While WeRide project our capability and values in physical AI onto autonomous vehicle dimension, a Robotaxi fleet is formed.

Through our Robotaxi application, we have successfully integrated foundation models, operating autonomous driving vehicles, data infrastructure, and commercial deployment together, forming a closed-loop evolving system that supports the scaling and evolution of physical AI capability of WeRide. While we project our physical AI capabilities onto mass production passenger vehicle, we have our ADAS business line, which are growing at a speed of 10x per year. Now let me walk through the progress across each of our business lines this quarter. First, about L4 and Robotaxi. I will start with our Robotaxi business line. We have reached a turning point in Robotaxi scale-up, supported by a positive UE in Guangzhou and the momentum of our overseas expansion.

Quarterly, Robotaxi revenue surpassed CNY 100 million. Mileage-based service fees now represent a bigger share of revenue, driving higher overall Robotaxi gross margin. In the Mideast, we accelerated our asset-light expansion. Our fleet stands at least approximately 600 vehicles, representing a 50% increase from the prior quarter end. This provides a broader foundation for scaling commercial operations across the region. Meanwhile, we now cover key core areas of Abu Dhabi and Dubai, with a target of full core city coverage by the year end. Our fleet has grown. Our technological capabilities and operational efficiency have improved, and our service footprint has expanded. Consequently, average daily rides, mileage per ride, and operating hours all rose, driving improvements in our unit economics.

In this market, we partner with e-hailing platform and local taxi operators, including Uber and TXAI. We tailor our autonomous driving solutions to local markets while complying with regional safety and traffic regulations. Asset-owning partners are incentivized to allocate more rides to us. Local fleet operators take care of day-to-day tasks like cleaning, enabling us to concentrate on enhancing autonomous driving capabilities and operational efficiency. Looking ahead, we expect our fleet in the Middle East to nearly double next year, and we also expect to achieve citywide driverless operations in a few major cities in this region. In Europe, we leverage the same asset-light partnership model deployed in the Middle East.

We secured Spain's first national L4 passenger autonomous vehicle permit in Madrid. Operational preparations are underway for commercial launch by year end. In Switzerland, leveraging the driverless permit secured last year, we rolled out public Robotaxi services in Zurich with partners SBB and STL. In Slovakia, with the support from the national ELEVATE initiative, road testing of the first batch of vehicles is underway. In Singapore, we have accumulatively provided more than 20,000 rides. This lays the groundwork for a future driverless commercial launch. In China, our driverless Robotaxi service in Guangzhou now covers Tianhe, Haizhu, and Huangpu. We will continue expanding into other core districts by year-end. On operating metrics, fleet size and service footprint keep expanding.

Guangzhou average daily rides per vehicle stayed flat quarter-over-quarter at 21, hitting a single-day peak of 33. This underpins positive unit economics. WeRide Go registered users jumped 143.5% quarter-on-quarter. Further, in late October, we officially launched our global insurance partnership. Allianz in Singapore and Ping An Property & Casualty Insurance joined as our first partners. Together, we are developing tailored insurance solutions for the full life cycle of L4 autonomous driving. These solutions address local regulatory requirements in China, Southeast Asia, the Mideast, and the European markets we are entering. They will support the global commercial rollout of Robotaxi. Our Robobus shares the same underlying autonomous driving technology stack as Robotaxi.

At the Zurich Airport, we have achieved full driverless Robobus operation. In Belgium, our Robobus public transit route continues to operate commercially on a stable basis. We are also advancing autonomous driving partnerships with public transportation operators, including Keolis in France. In Slovakia, Robobus is part of the country's national plan for multiple autonomous driving products. The fleet has arrived and begun testing. Our Robosweeper also expanded its presence in Singapore. We work with Chye Thiam Maintenance and RE Sustainability to deliver services across key locations in Singapore. I am also very proud to report that recently we have won eight titles in the China Intelligent Driving Competition.

In the two most recent competitions, our ADAS system, WRD 3.0, outperformed competing solutions with much more computational power. Our L2++/L3 business generates cash, builds our mass production capabilities, expanding our driving datasets, and strengthens WeRide's brand recognition among consumers. Last but not least, let me introduce our AI infrastructure subsidiary, Jingshuo. Building on closed-loop data capabilities developed through our autonomous driving operations, it provides pre-training data, post-training environments, and trusted verification across the full path from pre-training to continued learning. Through automated 3D reconstruction, multimodal alignment, and detailed labeling, it has built a substantial library of datasets covering home, retail, and industrial environments.

It now serves dozens of foundation model autonomous driving, embodied AI, and robotics companies worldwide with standard and customized datasets and skillsets, licensed data processing software, and post-training environments. Its orders under framework agreements now total several billion, and market demand for physical AI data keeps growing rapidly. Let me also explain the product stack. Jingshuo has three layers: EGOK, SkillForge, and Crucible. EGOK is a wearable multimodal data collection device. It keeps multiple data streams synchronized at a hardware level. SkillForge turns first-person task data into skillsets. These assets can be used for training, testing, and licensing. Crucible is an environment hub. It turns tasks into interactive environments that models can run in.

Results can be stored independently, and the environment can connect to post-training systems. Our strategy remains the same, one shared physical AI foundation that supports multiple businesses. The business draw on the same core technology and strength each other. This quarter, our overseas asset-light Robotaxi model is well established in the Middle East and continues to scale across Europe. In China, Guangzhou delivered positive UE. Together, these milestones represent a new stage, an inflection point for the scaling of our L4 business. Looking ahead to next 12 months, we have set out clear milestones that investors can hold us to.

Our first large-scale commercial launch in Europe, in Madrid, full coverage of core urban areas of Abu Dhabi and Dubai, and a Middle East fleet that nearby doubles next year. Driverless service in more core districts of Guangzhou and other cities in China, and continuing to converting Jingshuo's framework orders into revenue. Autonomous driving must respond within milliseconds and act with absolute precision. That requires purpose-built models that run on the vehicle in real time, trained and validated on vast amounts of real-world driving data. Ultimately, competition in autonomous driving and physical AI comes down to the strength of physical AI foundation and the ability to keep learning from data and integrating it.

Lasting advantages come from safe, reliable technology, a growing body of high-quality data that supports continuous improvement, and a healthy, profitable business model. With all of this in place, we are confident we will succeed on the journey ahead. With that, I will turn the call over to Xuan, our CFO and Head of International. She will walk you through our third quarter financial results. Thank you.

Xuan Li: Thank you, Xu. Hello, everyone. I will walk you through our financial and operating results for the third quarter of 2026. Let me start with three headlines. First, scale. Revenue grew 88% year-over-year to a record CNY 321.5 million, well ahead of street expectations. Second, the quality. Gross margin reached 43%, and overseas markets now contribute nearly half of the total revenue. That is high-quality revenue, recurring, contracted, and built to compound as our fleet grows. Third, discipline. Net loss narrowed 22.6% quarter-over-quarter to CNY 310 million, also better than street expectations. With CNY 4.7 billion in cash reserve, we are fully funded through to positive free cash flow. Revenue and gross margin.

The total revenue reached a record CNY 321.5 million, and overseas market led the way. Overseas revenue grew 171.5% to CNY 146.9 million, which is almost half of the rest of the revenue. All three businesses contributed. L4 revenue grew 47.2% year-over-year to CNY 168.8 million. L2++/L3 revenue grew nearly fivefold, and AI infrastructure revenue nearly doubled. Gross margin reached 43% this quarter. It rose 10.1 percentage point year-over-year and 5.5 percentage point quarter-over-quarter. This brought gross margin for the first nine months to 39.6%. The improvement came from a better revenue mix. Service revenue grew 102% year-over-year and now makes up 58% of total revenue. Two drivers stand out.

First, the overseas Robotaxi service fees, which we recognize on a net basis, made up a larger share of the revenue. Second, L2++ delivered under a license-based model carry a high double-digit gross margin. Note that this quarter's gross margin also benefit from a favorable revenue mix, which may vary from quarter to quarter. However, the underlying trend towards higher margin is very clear. Performance by businesses. L4 revenue grew 34.8% from last quarter. Within L4, Robotaxi revenue tripled, up 204% year-over-year to over CNY 100 million, and now makes up about 60% of the L4 revenue. More than 90% of the Robotaxi revenue came from overseas, led by the Middle East.

What matters most from our margin is how we earn this revenue. As our Middle East fleet grew 50% this quarter and operating hours and services area expanded, our mileage-based revenue sharing grew faster than total Robotaxi revenue. This is recurring asset-light revenue that grows with every ride. In terms of L2++/L3 business, the accumulative L2++ delivery exceeded 100,000 units by quarter end, ahead of the expectation we set at the beginning of the year. We expect to reach 500,000 units by the end of next year. Since we are paid through NRE and royalty, this business carries a high double-digit gross margin and generates operating cash flow at low marginal cost.

As it scales, this business strengthens our operating leverage as well. AI infrastructure revenue nearly doubled year-over-year, and Jingshuo now has several billion RMB in orders under framework agreements, giving us strong visibility into future growth. Demand is accelerating. Several lead customers who previously bought millions of hours of data are now considering tens of millions of hours over the next two years. This business is asset-light and cash-generative, and it also strengthens our own physical AI foundation platform. Turning to expenses, R&D expense rose 47.1% year-over-year, but only 7.1% quarter-over-quarter. R&D expenses as a percentage of revenue fell by 40.3 percentage points year-over-year and 42.7 percentage points quarter-over-quarter.

These are planned investments, mainly for the development of our next-generation Robotaxi, which we expect to further reduce BOM cost on a pre-installed basis once launched. R&D expenses this quarter also include costs related to campus recruiting in the summer and first-half performance bonuses. Our R&D team is now largely in place, and we do not plan large addition to R&D headcount. From here, our focus is on efficiency and output. Selling expense rose 39.2% year-over-year, but fell 9.3% quarter-over-quarter. They represented just 8.2% of the total revenue, down 2.9 percentage points year-over-year and 4.4 percentage points quarter-over-quarter. This reflects the efficiency of our market expansion and the benefit of operating leverage. Administrative expense were CNY 13.9 million this quarter.

This include a non-cash reversal of about CNY 49 million in share-based compensation expenses related to employee departures. Overall, our operating loss narrowed 12.3% year-over-year and 21.1% quarter-over-quarter to CNY 332.9 million. Net loss narrowed 22.6% quarter-over-quarter to CNY 310 million and was roughly flat year-over-year. Excluding share-based compensation and fair value changes, our adjusted net loss was CNY 336.5 million, essentially flat from last quarter, even as we continue to invest in our next-generation Robotaxi. As revenue continue to scale on a stable cost basis, we expect this to translate into a narrowing adjusted loss over time.

Now, let me address the three topics that investor has asked about: the cash use this quarter, the strength of our cash position, and also the potential equity dilution. We ended the quarter with CNY 4.7 billion in cash reserve. Our cash and cash equivalent fell by CNY 1.67 billion, but about CNY 1.07 billion of that was simply moved from cash to short-term investments, such as time deposits and treasury management products. In total, our cash reserve declined by about CNY 700 million. Most of this was actually timing, not run rate burn. We bought vehicles and kit ahead of the large overseas Robotaxi delivery in the fourth quarter, and some sales remains in receivable at the quarter end.

We also made prepayment for our next-generation Robotaxi and paid the first half-year bonuses. That working capital is now coming back. Receivable collections are well underway in the fourth quarter, and we expect to receive prepayment from customers in the fourth quarter as well. As a result, we expect our total cash reserves to remain stable in the fourth quarter. Looking ahead, we have tightened our spending plan and also prioritized our investments. Based on our current estimate of revenue and expenses for next year, we expect total cash burn to drop to about CNY 1 billion in 2027 and to decline further in 2028.

We remain on track for our first quarter of positive free cash flow in 2028 and positive free cash flow for the full year in 2029, and we expect to hold still more than CNY 1 billion in cash at that point. In short, our current cash fully funds our plan to self-sustain cash flow. All three businesses are contributing to this path. Overseas business generate recurring operating cash inflow, L2++ earn high-margin royalties, and Jingshuo is converting its growing framework orders into cash inflows as well. Last but not least, on equity dilution, let me be clear. We believe our share price does not reflect the value of our business, and we have acted on that belief.

Since March, we have repurchased over $95 million of our shares, meaningfully reduced our share count. With our plans fully funded, we see no reason to issue new share at a valuation that we believe does not reflect the value of this company. On the recent lockup expiry, under the Hong Kong Stock Exchange Chapter 18C rules, three senior executives were subject to a 12-month lockup following our Hong Kong listing last year. That lockup ended on November 5. The expiry covers shares held by three executives, Dr. Xu Han, our Founder and CEO, Dr. Yan Li, our Co-founder and CTO, and Dr. Hua Zhong, our Senior Vice President. None of the executives have ever sold shares in the company.

Dr. Xu Han's share remain fully locked up under his voluntary three-year commitment until October 2028. Management remains fully confident in WeRide's future. Given our strong result this quarter, we now expect 2026 revenue of at least CNY 1.1 billion, up more than 60% from 2025 and ahead of the current market expectations, street expectations. Looking ahead up to 2027, our growth drivers are clear, overseas fleet that we expect to double-scaling in Europe, and Middle East, and APAC. L2++ delivery growing towards 500,000 units and eventually converting framework orders into revenue. We expect to deliver this growth while cutting cash burn to about CNY 1 billion next year.

Over time, we expect our commercial fleet to grow roughly tenfold every three years. Faster growth, higher margins, and lower cash burn. That is our path to self-sustain cash flow and long-term value for the shareholders. That concludes my financial review. We are now ready to take questions. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. As a reminder, we only accept questions in the English language line. To ask a question, please dial into the English line and then press star, one on your telephone touch-tone keypad. If you have any follow-on question, please re-enter the queue. Thank you. We will now take our first question. From the line of Paul Gong from UBS. Please go ahead.

Paul Gong: Thanks, Xu and Xuan, for taking my question. I have two questions. The first question is regarding the scalability of the Robotaxi fleets in a sustainable way. How should we consider the comparison versus the global leaders like Waymo and Tesla? My second question is regarding the competition in Europe. We are seeing more and more Chinese Robotaxi companies are getting into the Europe market. How should we see the rising competition potentially in that market? My two questions. Thank you.

Xu Han: Okay, I will take the first two questions. So first is about scalability compared with Waymo and Tesla. Basically, how do we answer the competition from Waymo and Tesla? Second is more specific to the European market. As everybody know, Waymo also entering European market, and what is the competitive landscape in Europe, and how will WeRide compete against Waymo? Okay. First of all, I think any interesting field or profitable field will be full of competition. And I think we respect Waymo and Tesla a lot. They are tech giants, two great companies. We are honored to compete against them. But the thing is, I think we have our competitive edge.

So, I believe very few companies worldwide can manage the full process from driverless operation and the local compliance to commercial delivery. Of course, Waymo and Tesla, they have already achieved certain results, but I believe the market is large enough for multiple players, and WeRide is definitely among one of the major players in the global market. Let's talk about our competitive edge, comparing to Waymo and Tesla. First of all, for global market, I think there's one thing I want to mention, that is our technology. Our L4 system combines a one-stage end-to-end model with dedicated safety architecture. That, to my best knowledge, is superior to other companies' technology. We have built-in redundancy and independent rule-based safety layer.

Basically, if you talk about Tesla is basically end-to-end model, and Waymo, according to our best knowledge, is still based, lots of based on the rules. WeRide's approach is a kind of marriage of the two approach, and we can adapt quickly to a new environment. The safety architecture meets strict standards, like European standard. This is our one technology advance. Second is about the scalability. If you look at the efficiency and hardware cost, you will find out, especially for international deployment, we are in a much better position. Our vehicles are cheaper, and our hardware are more cost-efficient, and we can leverage on the superior supply chain of China auto industry.

Regarding European market, we have another advantage, that is early entry. We actually entered the China and the Middle East market very early, and now we entered Europe market very early. We got the Spain's first national L4 operating permit. With all of this first mover advance, I think we expect to remain our leading position in European market. The last but not the least, that is our capital efficiency. We work with partners like Uber and Grab under an asset-light model, and we don't need to build our own customer acquisition, dispatch service, and insurance system from scratch. This is a great advantage over Tesla and Waymo. They all build up their things on their own.

Waymo and Tesla, they are kind of asset-intensive model. With all of these kind of aforementioned factors, I think we are really in a leading position. Again, as you have noticed, WeRide as a startup and actually founded in the year of 2017, we are much younger company compared to the other two. Overall, if you look at our deployment footprint, look at our scalability, we are comparable to the other two companies, and we are confident with our final results, and we are confident with our final positions in this very competitive field. That's my answer.

Paul Gong: Thank you very much. That is very helpful.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of Tim Hsiao from Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tim Hsiao: Hi, Xu and Xuan. Thank you for taking my question. I have one question. As you mentioned, you have demonstrated positive unit economics overseas and validated a business model that appears to work for both WeRide and local partners. I wonder when do you think the scaling will speed up from here, and what needs to happen for deployment volumes to accelerate meaningfully over the next few years? Thank you.

Xuan Li: Okay, thank you, Tim. I will take this question. Our overseas Robotaxi business is very healthy, and it is profitable for us and also for the partner. For us, we have two parts of the business. At initial delivery, we sell the Robotaxi, which bundled with about six years of recurring mileage-based revenue sharing. So each vehicle gives us upfront revenue and also a long-term recurring income stream. It is also asset-light for us. Our platform partners and local partners who own the vehicles, they have very strong incentive to maximize utilization. So we focus on the technology and the functions that makes the vehicle truly driverless, and then next day remote assistance, and so we need less capital.

We actually can move very fast. On the scaling part, it follows the same principle. In every market, the path from testing with safety driver to fully driverless operation usually takes at least, like, say, a year in major cities. That is how long it takes just to complete all the required testing procedures and build trust with regulators, especially in Europe. For now, we have also observed since we started to earn regulatory confidence in multiple market, now we can see the entering new market actually moves a little bit faster than the last one. The trend is clear.

To answer your question on the scaling up, this year, the number of vehicles we have deployed overseas has already exceeded our own expectations. Like, say, the Middle East fleet grew 50% in one quarter to about 600 vehicles, and we expect it to reach somewhere around 800 to 1,000 by year end and double next year. In Europe, we will have more than 100 L4 vehicles by end of this year, which is going to be the largest Alpha fleet in entire Europe. Our main constraint is not really the tech, but it is really just the permit timing. The demand is already locked in. Here is a very important number.

We have binding contracts for about 3,000 Robotaxis globally as of today, signed with multiple partners for delivery in near term, as long as we can get a permit. As the permit comes through, those will directly translate into revenues for our overseas business. The demand is there. We are working very hard to earn the regulatory trust as fast as we can so that we can scale up. As for now, Xu also just mentioned, we are already Uber's largest driverless partner outside the U.S. Also, we are the largest driverless partner for multiple platforms. We can see the positive trends already there.

What is more important, our industry-leading safety record overseas and also the largest overseas fleet, all of this speaking for itself. Those track records is our long-term moat, and our reputation, our safety procedure, and long-term partnership across the local ecosystem are very hard to replicate, and they are what allows us to scale really globally. I hope that answers the question, Tim.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of Jiajie Shen from JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Jiajie Shen: Yes, thank you, Xu and Xuan, for taking my question. I have one question. You just mentioned that L4 Robotaxi operations in one Chinese city have turned profitable. So what are your plans for expanding into other cities in China, and could you also share your global Robotaxi expansion plans for year-end and next year? Thank you.

Xu Han: Okay. I will take this question. So, this quarter, Guangzhou achieved a positive UE at a city level for a full quarter for the first time. I think this is a great milestone. It shows our operational model works. Cost structure, dispatch system can support profitable business. For China expansion, I believe a policy environment is moving in a clearly positive direction. Just last week, or I'm sorry, this week, I think, the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen, President Xi highlighted autonomous driving as one of the most frontier technology in China, and the central government will give strong support.

As national policy become more supportive and standardized, operator with mature technology and strong safety records, we will definitely copy our model to the rest of the city. Now, our current priority in Guangzhou is to keep growing the fleet, expand service areas, and raise utilization in Guangzhou. As policy open up for more cities, we will simply replicate this model and expect to reach positive unit economics in multiple cities. That's our plan. Basically, keep on sharpening our technology and the models and the efficiencies in Guangzhou since it's already profitable. Once other city open up the policy, we just quickly copy to other cities.

As we achieve positive UE in China, we want to also quickly expand to the rest of the world. In the Middle East, we will keep growing our fleet and strengthening our market position. In Europe, we are building a full commercial operation in Madrid, which is one of top 3 largest ride-hailing cities in Europe. In future, we are currently working on Switzerland, Denmark, and Slovakia. Next year, we expect the Middle East to keep expanding and Europe to become another major growth driver as we bring Madrid model to other European markets and with supportive policies. Overall, we really aim to grow our operating Robotaxi fleet roughly 10x every three years.

But our priority is positive unit economics, healthy cash flow, and sustainable operations. So, that's our major focus, and we are very confident about our plans. Thank you. That's my answer.

Jiajie Shen: Yeah, that's very clear. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of Ming Hsun Lee from Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Ming Hsun Lee: Hi, Xu, Xuan. I have two questions. My first question, how would you describe the strategic partners with Uber? What are your plans for the partnership? Thank you.

Xu Han: Sorry, I forgot to unmute my microphone. I will take this question. Uber is definitely our core strategic partner and a major shareholder. I believe the strength of WeRide and Uber are actually complementary. WeRide bring the L4 technology, the safety system, and a proven record to regulators. Uber actually bring its global ride-based platform and resources. Together, I think we form an alliance that is unparalleled, and I don't foresee any other alliance or competitors can compete in the alliance of WeRide and Uber. The Middle East has proven that model. Today, we operate Uber's largest driverless fleet outside the U.S., and we expect our Middle East fleet to grow into thousands of vehicles soon.

Europe is a very big opportunity, and we launched Europe's first driverless commercial Robobus service on public road in France, but we are more excited about Madrid to come. With Uber, we are making good progress in Madrid, and we expect to launch in several more European cities next year. We look forward to sharing on the relevant information once we announce. Our model also work with multiple platform and local partners, and we can move into each market with right partners. Also, I want to emphasize, we have an asset-light model, which is already proven profitable and workable. Our focus is currently on high utilization and more efficient operation. Okay, that's my answer to your question.

Operator: Thank you. We have another question from-

Xu Han: So, we answer the second question, Jen? That is my answer. Okay, I see. Second question, I think Jen may answer. Okay.

Operator: Well, I think Ming has not asked the second question yet. Ming, please go ahead.

Ming Hsun Lee: Okay. Yeah. Thank you. Yeah, so recent advances in frontier AI have sparked this discussion around whether autonomous driving could eventually be solved by general purpose AI models. How do you view the long-term impact of the foundation models on the Robotaxi industry, and where will be sustainable competitive advantages reside as AI capability continue to evolve?

Xuan Li: Xu, you want to take the question?

Xu Han: I think let you take the question, or I take the question. Who wants? Okay, I will take the question.

Xuan Li: Yeah, it is on frontier LLM, I think. It is better.

Xu Han: I understand this, but I take this question. Yeah, I just feel like, yeah, a little bit due to the jet lag, I am a little bit kind of tired, but I think I will answer this question. So first of all, it is a very heated discussion and debate, so it is kind of Thank you for this great question. I think this question is really great. In a broad way, you can say everything can be replaced by AI. Nowadays, whatever, we cannot safely say that anything cannot be replaced by AI.

But if you look into details, okay, so we can see that the general-purpose model are very good at high-level tasks like reasoning and coding, but controlling a car is completely different problem. It is just like, why we believe the humanoid robot can replace all the top-level surgeon to do the surgery for patients, okay? It is still in a sci-fi movie. In a recent public test, even the most advanced general-purpose model could barely complete a single lap of empty parking lot. Driving is a matter of life and death. The system has to respond within milliseconds with absolute precision, and there's no room for mistakes. Let me emphasize, there's no room for mistakes.

Auto-grade chips with high power limit. This kind of thing really requires lots of technology to really work on it. All of the hardware for the autonomous driving vehicle are purposely built. I don't think a general AI model can be run on this kind of platform within next three or four years. These are just some general discussion. People talk about in a general way, but come to the field, and we studied large language model very carefully. By the way, I think I'm in a position to say so because my background is in really AI. I think, for the general-purpose build foundation model, they currently don't have a chance.

Because we have to have a very compact model on it, and the precision is key. Over time, foundation model may gradually improve, but there's a long way to go. I think in the near future, as a five-year framework, I don't see any chance for this general-purpose AI can write a autonomous driving algorithm and replace the current algorithm. Within five years, if you look at our plan, we have already deployed our Robotaxi fleet, covered global market. We will keep an eye on this general-purpose algorithm. As I mentioned, we have built out all the physical AI-relevant infrastructure. If the general-purpose LLM can work, I think we are among the first group of companies who adopt this technology.

Overall, we embrace this technology, and we are confident this company will be the first pioneer who adopt this technology, and we will remain as a leading position. As the first mover company, we will remain at our current position and enjoy the consequential profit and revenue. That's my answers to this question. Thank you. Great question. Very insightful.

Xuan Li: Just to add on a little bit more to this question. A better model doesn't alone, it doesn't put the driverless car on the road. What we do quite intensively is discussing with the regulator. Regulator, they need to approve a validated system in each specific market, and it's not the model who's doing this. The real heavy lifting is to build the trust, integrating the software, hardware, testing across cities, countries, and proving safety over millions of kilometers. Then we have to operate it at scale on everyday basis. That's why we have spent the years to build. Now we have permit in nine countries. We are running in 13 countries, in 60 cities.

That's actually a key moat that we have building over the years. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of Yuqian Ding from HSBC. Please go ahead.

Yuqian Ding: Thank you, team. Yuqian here. It is actually a two-parting question on the China L2++ market. We are seeing the competition is getting tense, OEMs are struggling, probably more pressure on pricing. How would management evaluating the competition landscape going forward? Could you also share your order growth as in both volume and pricing term? Thank you.

Xu Han: I think I will take this question. First of all, I have to admit, the competition is intensive. Automakers are very cost conscious, and the industry really want to bring smart driving to more buyers. We see a big opportunity, because currently the urban navigation or autopilot penetration is still low, and we see a big market, big opportunity. There is plenty of room and long-term growth. I think our goal is to make smart driving, including urban navigation, available to everyone, both in China and for the overseas market. We can do that because our cost is significantly lower than our peers. Our one-stage end-to-end solution actually just shares the technology we developed with our L4 driverless operation.

You can see the track record. We won eight titles in China's intelligent driving competition, which basically means our ADAS system is superior. It is much better than our competitors. We have got more than 20 mass production deployments, and we have more volumes to come. We are really confident, actually, in future for the growth. Overall, I think L2++ plays a very clear role in our strategy, and it builds our brand with our consumers and grows our driving data. We basically use our L2++ application and our L4 Robotaxi operation leverage onto each other, sharing the data and help each other to improve the algorithms.

In the future, the goal of development of L2++ is it requires a higher and higher computational platform, which can adopt more and more advanced L4 level technology, which WeRide have developed over the past 10 years and is one of the best company in L4. Overall, I think WeRide will remain its leading position in ADAS, and more and more OEMs will adopt our system. I look forward to take even larger market share in ADAS market. As I mentioned before, the penetration for NOA will keep on growing, I think, to 100%, because most of the people, they do not want to drive by themselves. They just want to rely on the system help to drive.

Overall, with our technology, we are confident that we will remain at our current leading position. Thank you for this question.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of Yuan Tao from CSC. Please go ahead.

Yuan Tao: Hi. Good evening. I have a question about the UE. WeRide achieved positive unit economics in Guangzhou this quarter. Can you walk us through how you define UE and what costs are included, and roughly how they break down? Thank you.

Xuan Li: I will take this question. Okay. Reaching unit economic breakeven is actually a really important milestone for us. I will be very precise about what it includes. On the revenue side, we count the net ride-hailing revenue after the refunds. On the cost side, we include all the major cost items. That includes vehicle depreciation, including battery, all the way to autonomous driving hardwares, and also the charging, the salary for remote, and also the ground supporting staff. Also, there is cleaning, maintenance, insurance, parking, network, and telecom fees. Everything is included. Slightly less than half of the total cost goes to the vehicle depreciation related, and the rest is other items.

That is a very comprehensive measure of all the cost items. In Guangzhou, we achieved the positive UE for the first time, with an average order of 21 daily order per vehicle. There are three things that are actually driving this. First of all, it is the high utilization, longer average trip distance, and also a higher efficient staff-to-vehicle ratio for both remote assistance and ground support. We will keep improving those ratios so that the per-vehicle labor costs stay as low as possible. Also, when the fleet is growing, we just want to make sure that the per-vehicle labor cost can be really low.

Like I say, we can already achieve a positive UE in Guangzhou, and for overseas, the structure will be even more attractive. Under our asset-light business model, the partners own vehicles, and then we do not carry the CapEx for the vehicles. On top of that, we bring what we learned in China to our overseas markets. For now, we have already improved on the remote assistant efficiency in the Middle East to more than one to 10, and we are also optimizing the dispatch system, the maintenance process, and the fleet management playbooks. In short, China is one of the most demanding operating environments in the world.

Applying this experience abroad helps us to, and our partners as well, to streamlining the cost and launch new markets faster. This matters even more in places like Europe, where the initial launch, like say, the labor and energy costs can be very high. So yeah, this is a key milestone for us to reach, unit breakeven in China. Yeah. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. We will now take the next question from the line of Dongbin Han from Huatai Securities. Please go ahead.

Xuan Li: Actually, I think we are running out of time. Maybe we can just take one more question, one last question.

Dongbin Han: Okay, thank you. Hi, management. Due to time limits, I will keep it brief. Congratulations to this strong quarter. My two questions. First, do you have enough cash to reach breakeven in 2029? Which expenses are temporary and which will be recurring? Second, will the company issue new shares or conduct a placement under the current share price? Thanks so much.

Xuan Li: Okay, I will be brief about this. To answer the first question, yes, we have enough cash to reach breakeven in 2029. Yes, like we just mentioned over the call, we ended the quarter with CNY 4.7 billion in cash reserve. More importantly, in the fourth quarter, the receivable collection and the prepayment should keep our cash reserve roughly stable as the same as now. We expect cash burn to also fall to around CNY 1 billion in 2027, and it will decline even further in 2028. In 2028, that is when we expect we will have the first-ever quarterly positive free cash flow.

With that, if everything goes according to the plan, in 2029, while we can expect positive free cash flow for the full year, we still have more than CNY 1 billion in cash. That is the runway, what we are thinking about this. For the. Just now you also asked about the temporary items. The one-off items will be, like say, for the last quarter, it is the first half performance bonus and upfront payment for our next generation Robotaxi. Those are the one-off. The stage-specific investment, like say, the computing cluster, we will still build some, especially in Europe and in the Middle East, depending on. It is actually really according to the deployment schedule.

Those costs are spread over a much larger revenue base. What the recurring costs will going to be, like say, the R&D stuff and then the ongoing, the model training, those will be the ongoing recurring items. We think we validate unit economic in each market before we really scale in the market, so that will keep us the cash burn under control. In short, we do have full confidence in reaching breakeven in 2029, and the revenue growth really rallies and continues. The last question, I think you also asked about the issue new share.

As we just mentioned, we think the current valuation does not reflect the company's true value, and we will not carry out the issuance or placement at the current valuation. We won't do it. Our priority is really to improve cash flow through the business itself, scaling over using our asset-light L4 business overseas, our growing L2++/L3 production deliveries, and also from Jingshuo data set services. Those will help us to move steadily towards positive cash flow. Thank you.

Operator: Thank you. Due to time constraints, I will conclude the call today. Thank you for your participation in today's conference. This does conclude the program. You may now disconnect.

#3149. Salesforce vs. ServiceNow: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Salesforce trades at a lower forward P/E than ServiceNow, yet ServiceNow is growing revenue faster, forcing investors to weigh price against momentum.

By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:27PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Salesforce ›

The shift toward enterprise automation and artificial intelligence has created a fierce battle between two cloud software titans. Investors choosing between Salesforce (CRM -1.47%) and ServiceNow (NOW -1.42%) must decide which platform offers better value.

Salesforce dominates the customer relationship management space, helping businesses track every client interaction. ServiceNow specializes in streamlining back-office workflows, from IT support to HR tasks. Both companies are now racing to integrate generative AI into their ecosystems, making this a pivotal comparison for investors seeking growth in tech stocks.

Salesforce provides cloud-based software that connects sales, marketing, and IT on a single platform to serve over 150,000 companies. It has recently prioritized AI integration through a major partnership with Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) for "Copilotforce," which combines customer context with AI experiences. The company continues expanding its reach through acquisitions such as Braze (BRZE +0.09%) to deepen engagement. Salesforce serves businesses of all sizes globally, and no single customer accounts for more than 10% of its total revenue.

In the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, revenue reached approximately $43.9 billion, representing growth of nearly 11.2% over the prior period. The company also generated net income of roughly $9.7 billion, which reflects a net margin of close to 22%. This growth trend has been supported by a steady increase in revenue from $34.9 billion just two years ago. The business focuses on maintaining profitability while scaling its cloud ecosystem and proprietary AI tools.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.3x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, a measure of how well a company covers short-term debts with short-term assets, is approximately 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $14.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

ServiceNow offers an AI platform designed to automate enterprise work across departments including IT, human resources, and finance. The company focuses on large enterprise clients, ending recent periods with over 600 customers spending more than $5 million annually. It maintains strategic partnerships with Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) and Accenture (ACN +1.19%) to drive AI-driven workflow integrations for its 8,700 total customers. This strategy targets a growing presence in the public sector and large organizations seeking efficient digital transformation.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $15.4 billion, marking revenue growth of approximately 21.8% over the preceding year. ServiceNow reported net income of nearly $1.4 billion for this period, yielding a net margin of approximately 9.4%. While its net margin is lower than its rival, the company has consistently increased its top line from $9.0 billion two years prior. This expansion reflects robust demand for workflow automation tools across global markets.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.2x. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term obligations using liquid assets, is roughly 1.0x, and free cash flow reached nearly $4.6 billion in the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 35.9% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Salesforce faces intense competition from established software vendors and AI-native firms entering the customer relationship management space. Integrating large-scale acquisitions like Braze involves execution risks that could disrupt operations if not managed carefully. The company also navigates cybersecurity threats and potential volatility from shifting its pricing models toward consumption-based structures.

ServiceNow must prove it can continue competing effectively as the AI market evolves rapidly. The company relies on third-party cloud providers and faces regulatory scrutiny related to its growing government contracting business. Additionally, any failure to realize benefits from its aggressive merger and acquisition strategy could impact future growth prospects if integration costs exceed the value gained.

Salesforce appears more attractively priced on a relative basis, carrying a lower Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates and a lower P/S ratio measuring value against sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

I'd go with ServiceNow. Management expects its AI products to reach $1.7 billion in yearly contracts by the end of this year, and they run on software that big companies rely on for everyday work like IT and HR requests. That software is a very sticky product, with an impressive 98% renewal rate, meaning almost all customers sign up again.

ServiceNow's AI business is growing fast, and overall sales are still rising rapidly. The stock plunged after its latest earnings report, as investors worried about slower growth in future contracts and about AI hurting software companies. But management has raised its AI goal twice this year, and the drop leaves the shares well below where they traded before.

To be fair to Salesforce, it is the cheaper stock and it is buying back a lot of its own shares. Its AI products are also catching on. But its sales are growing more slowly, and part of that growth came from buying another company. For long-term investors, ServiceNow offers a fast-growing AI business on top of software customers rarely leave, at a lower price after the recent sell-off.

#3148. What Security Teams Still Get Wrong About Asset Visibility

Yochai Corem is GM of Exposure Management at Check Point Software.

Organizations have more asset data than ever, but turning that data into a reliable view of what they own, operate and expose remains difficult.

A server appears in three tools with different identifiers. A cloud workload has an owner who has left the business. A forgotten website remains online after the campaign that funded it has ended. Each leaves security teams with information they still have to investigate before they can act.

Security leaders should judge asset visibility by how reliably it supports a decision. A useful inventory helps teams establish what an asset does, who is responsible for it, how it is protected and what should happen when a problem appears.

Several familiar assumptions prevent organizations from reaching that standard.

An incomplete configuration management database (CMDB) should prompt a review of how records are created, updated and retired.

Start by defining its purpose. The CMDB should record the systems, services and dependencies needed to manage business operations, with accountable owners and lifecycle status. Detailed security telemetry can remain in specialist systems, linked through reliable identifiers. An impersonating website belongs in an external threat register connected to the affected brand.

Then identify which sources can reveal missing records. Cloud platforms, endpoint management, identity providers, vulnerability scanners and procurement systems can each expose inconsistencies. Buying a service should trigger registration; retiring it should trigger checks that access, infrastructure and records have been removed.

Reconciliation should reflect the pace of change. I would set a daily reconciliation target for cloud and endpoint feeds; use deployment and retirement events to trigger updates; and review unresolved discrepancies weekly. Quarterly ownership reviews can supplement those checks.

An asset without an owner needs an interim accountable team and an escalation deadline. “Unknown” should describe an investigation in progress.

The modern attack surface spans internal infrastructure, cloud workloads, software as a service (SaaS), internet-facing systems, supplier connections and the organization’s broader digital presence.

Those categories need different forms of accountability. Infrastructure teams may manage servers, cloud teams manage workloads and business application owners sponsor SaaS services. Marketing or regional teams may control domains and social accounts. Supplier relationships require a business sponsor alongside technical oversight.

Security should establish a review and response process across those boundaries. A newly discovered domain needs ownership verification and an assessment of what it hosts. An unfamiliar SaaS service needs checks on its users, data and access. A fraudulent social account needs investigation and a disruption process.

Review frequency should follow exposure and change, with continuous discovery where practical and scheduled reviews for ownership, supplier access and dormant services. This broader scope aligns with the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s (NIST) inclusion of hardware, software, services and supplier services in asset management.

Leaders can test this assumption by following a newly discovered asset through the security process.

Does discovery trigger checks for required endpoint protection, vulnerability scanning and an accountable owner? Does an unmanaged internet-facing system reach someone authorized to restrict or remove it? Can the organization confirm that the resulting action occurred?

These outcomes show whether visibility operates as a security control. The Center for Internet Security’s (CIS) Control 1 connects inventory management with identifying and addressing unauthorized or unmanaged assets.

Useful measures include the time taken to assign ownership, the proportion of applicable assets covered by required controls and the age of unresolved discrepancies. A growing inventory count provides little reassurance when newly discovered systems remain unmanaged.

Additional tools introduce additional records, each with its own identifiers, timestamps and assumptions.

Effective reconciliation requires explicit rules. Stable cloud resource identifiers or device identifiers should take precedence over an Internet Protocol (IP) address that may change or be reused. Records need source and freshness information so teams can distinguish a current observation from a stale entry.

Organizations also need rules for conflicting fields. The identity system may establish who uses a device, while a service registry identifies the team accountable for the application it supports. Those relationships should remain distinguishable.

Cyber asset attack surface management (CAASM) can support this work. Organizations can also improve CMDB integrations, use cloud asset inventories and service catalogs, or build reconciliation workflows in their existing data platforms. The operational requirements remain consistent: reliable matching, clear authority for each field and a process for resolving exceptions.

Discovery should initiate a decision about management, protection or retirement.

A forgotten website needs an owner to confirm whether it still serves a business purpose. A vulnerable application needs assessment of its exposure, dependencies and operational constraints before a response is selected.

That decision should remain traceable through completion. If a service is retired, verify that it is no longer reachable. If a security control is applied, confirm that it covers the intended asset. Updating the inventory should accompany the operational change.

This ongoing connection between asset information and action also underpins continuous threat exposure management (CTEM).

CTEM depends on this discipline throughout scoping, discovery, prioritization, validation and mobilization.

An unknown asset cannot enter the prioritization process. A known asset without business context is difficult to rank. Missing dependencies weaken assessments of attack paths and change impact. An unknown owner delays action, while stale records undermine confirmation that an exposure has been reduced.

CAASM and external attack surface management (EASM) can support these stages by reconciling internal records and discovering internet-facing assets. Their value depends on the ownership, decision rules and response processes surrounding them.

Security leaders should expect asset visibility to connect discovery with accountable action. Every significant asset needs enough current context for someone to determine its protection requirements, address its exposures and verify the result. That is how a reliable inventory helps reduce the opportunities available to an attacker.​

There are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel plans than the groupings suggest.

Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

Each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

Through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

Through Dec. 31, 2027, these 10 Oneworld Alliance hubs count toward bonus points and status points. Qualifying layovers also count toward the destination challenge, so you don’t necessarily need to make these cities your final stop.

If you frequently travel internationally or have any upcoming flights through any of these airports, including qualifying layovers, Global Locals might be a fit for you.

#3145. Teradyne: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Memory supply constraints are forcing chipmakers to increase test volume per wafer, a potential tailwind for Teradyne's core business.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:30PM EST

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, Teradyne (TER -9.96%) announced total company revenue reached $1.3 billion as artificial intelligence demand expanded across all business lines. For long-term investors, the expansion of automated test equipment (custom hardware used to verify semiconductor chips) into data center infrastructure creates a multiyear growth runway.

Hyperscalers and chipmakers adopt dual vendor strategies (buying test equipment from two suppliers) to secure capacity and avoid supply chain delays. That shift gives Teradyne a direct path to capture market share in high performance compute chips where rivals previously held dominant positions.

Severe memory supply constraints force chipmakers to use lower stack heights in high bandwidth memory (specialized vertical memory stacks for fast data processing). Lower stack heights require more total stacks to process the same wafer volume, directly increasing the volume of performance tests Teradyne conducts.

As data center connections shift toward optical networking, handling and alignment requirements remain in flux. Teradyne forms open, nonexclusive partnerships with specialized equipment vendors to build complete test cells. This approach speeds high-volume production for next-generation data center architectures.

Quarterly sales holding above $1.2 billion reflect a structural step change in operational scale. Teradyne expands manufacturing capacity and dual-sources component suppliers to meet artificial intelligence infrastructure demand.

Heavy research investments and open partner ecosystems protect technical leadership across test and robotics segments. Management watches customer qualification pacing and supply lead times as semiconductor capital spending expands through 2028.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 28, 2026, ONEOK (OKE -2.48%) raised its full-year financial guidance for the third time this year after reporting record natural gas processing volumes in the Permian Basin region of West Texas and New Mexico. A debt paydown and an integrated pipeline footprint give the company room to fund growth projects while returning capital to shareholders.

The company paid off nearly $5.5 billion of debt during the third quarter after completing a $9 billion equity transaction. Management is using that balance sheet relief to shift its leverage target to 3.25 times debt-to-EBITDA or lower, where EBITDA represents earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a metric measuring core operating profitability.

Total raw feed throughput for natural gas liquids (NGLs), which are liquid hydrocarbons such as propane and ethane, grew 6% year over year. The company stored raw feed while waiting for its Medford fractionator facility to restart in mid-December, pushing those associated earnings into early 2027.

Surging power demand from electric utilities and technology data centers is driving long-term commitments for natural gas pipeline capacity. ONEOK recently locked in a 10-year contract to move 250 million cubic feet per day of natural gas to power a 1-gigawatt plant.

Producer drilling activity is building across the Bakken and Mid-Continent regions, giving management direct momentum into year-end. ONEOK's integrated network connects wellhead gathering to Gulf Coast export facilities, protecting cash flow through long-term fee contracts and active commodity hedging while management tracks drilling discipline and regional pricing differentials.

With debt paydowns opening up balance sheet room and recent acquisitions adding Permian scale, ONEOK is positioning its system to capture expanding power generation and export demand.

TL;DR: Mortgage rates eased today, but borrowing costs are still expensive for many home buyers.

Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.)

A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a big reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

If PCE shows inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you plan to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

» Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

» Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis

If you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

#3140. Take-Two Interactive vs. Anthropic: Which Market-Moving Stock Is the Better Buy?

Take-Two and Anthropic grabbed investor attention in the latter part of the week.

By Will Healy – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:33PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›

Take-Two Interactive (TTWO +0.65%) and Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) are arguably the two stocks that generated the most excitement this week.

Anthropic launched its IPO this week, as its Claude artificial intelligence (AI) assistant has generated investor excitement and driven massive revenue growth. That may have been overshadowed by gamers who have awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), possibly since Take-Two released GTA 5 in 2013.

Despite that anticipation and the likely boost to Take-Two stock, I believe Anthropic is the better buy, and here's why.

Admittedly, Take-Two might be a more obvious choice since the anticipation for GTA 6 likely predates Anthropic's 2021 founding.

With that waiting game now over, Take-Two subsidiary Rockstar Games revealed that it sold 32.5 million copies of the game on day one, generating $3.79 billion in revenue. That is huge considering that the company reported $3 billion in the first six months of fiscal 2027 (ended Sept. 30). That was game-changing, figuratively and literally, for Take-Two stock, which also reported an 8% year-over-year revenue decline during the same period.

Furthermore, net losses have left it without a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio. Still, according to analysts, this sales boost puts Take-Two on track for an estimated 27% yearly revenue gain in fiscal 2027 and a return to profitability. That recovery could make investors more willing to pay its 30 forward P/E ratio.

Unfortunately, game releases are one-off events, and such temporary sales bumps tend to run their course quickly. Consequently, analysts believe the entertainment stock's revenue growth will slow to 6% in fiscal 2028, making the release unlikely to change the company's long-term value proposition.

In contrast, Anthropic's gains are on track to be more than one-time. Companies from nearly all sectors of the economy are scrambling to incorporate AI into their businesses. This has greatly benefited Claude, which has stood toe-to-toe with the competition from OpenAI's ChatGPT and Alphabet's (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) Google Gemini.

Its financials confirm its fast-growing popularity. The $33 billion it generated in the first nine months of 2026 far exceeded the $2.5 billion it reported during the same period in 2025.

Moreover, although it lost $104 billion during the first three quarters of 2026, $94 billion of that loss resulted from changes in the fair value of convertible notes. The operating losses were less than $1.3 billion of that total loss, suggesting it could turn an operating profit in the foreseeable future.

Additionally, even after giving back most of its IPO pop, its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio is around 45, far more than Take-Two's sales multiple of 6.

For next year, analysts estimate 135% revenue growth. At current prices, that would likely reduce its sales multiple over time, potentially pushing Anthropic stock higher.

Between Take-Two and Anthropic, I recommend the latter.

Indeed, the GTA 6 release should put Take-Two on a firmer financial footing. Unfortunately, that sales bump is likely to be temporary, suggesting it cannot rely on one new game release to improve Take-Two's long-term value proposition.

In contrast, Anthropic has benefited from tremendous AI demand, so much so that it will likely report triple-digit revenue growth for the foreseeable future. That probably means that even with an elevated valuation, it should deliver higher returns to investors over time.
